messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: autoscaler controller failing to reconcile for /hosted/inference-pool-3 — sustained CPU > 95% on control plane, ~12% of requests returning 504 to users. Paging @oncall-sre. details: https://alerts.redwood.local/1837605120 :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: seeing the page, I'm on it. grabbing logs from control-plane and node-exporter now. anyone still seeing 504s?

maria (sre): yep - customer-facing error spike started ~08:12 UTC. Error pattern looks like upstream 504 from gateway, not model kernel OOMs.

aj (runtime): adding context — we pushed a tweak to the HPA config for inference-pool-3 yesterday (window -> 60s) to reduce thrash. can that be related?

kevin (infra): possible. the controller has an RBAC flake in the latest rollout that prevents scaling events when nodes hit cordon cycles. i'm pulling the controller logs.

oncall-sre: quick mitigation idea: disable the HPA controller for that pool so nodes stop cycling, and scale the pool manually to add capacity. wil try helm rollback for the controller to previous image.

aj (runtime): i can flip routing to send a small % of traffic to a warm fallback model variant (model-small-v2) to reduce load on the heavy hosts. will patch route if infra confirms rollback.

kevin (infra): helm rollback started for autoscaler-controller -> release autoscaler-1.3.4 (stable). running: `helm rollback autoscaler 2`

ops-bot: Command run by kevin: helm rollback autoscaler 2 — status: in_progress

oncall-sre: while that's rolling, manually scaling pool nodes +3: `kubectl scale --replicas=8 deployment/inference-pool-3`

maria (sre): observed request error rate drop from 12% -> 2% after the manual scale and rollback. latency tail still elevated but errors falling. :white_check_mark:

aj (runtime): started a 10% route split to model-small-v2: `redwood route update /generate --split 90:10 --variants=model-large-v1,model-small-v2` — seeing higher client latency on small model but it's stabilizing.

oncall-sre: good. continuing to monitor for 30m. capturing logs and traces into the incident doc. anyone seeing anything else?

kevin (infra): controller pods showed repeated 403s talking to the api-server — confirming RBAC regression in last change. logs: ```2027-02-12T08:11:59Z controller error: forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:infra:autoscaler" cannot ...```

maria (sre): filing immediate bug: INF-5234 (Autoscaler RBAC regression). assigning to @kevin.

product-lead: customer impact note — live usage for a handful of enterprise tenants saw increased error rates for 6–12 minutes, some calls retried by client libs. flagging for CS outreach.

oncall-sre: thanks. we're going to close the page as mitigated but need a postmortem and follow-ups. provisional severity: SEV2.

incident-bot: Incident 1837605120 marked mitigated at 1837606920 by oncall-sre — summary: autoscaler RBAC regression caused controller to stop reconciling -> node churn -> gateway 504s. manual scale + helm rollback + traffic split to fallback model mitigated.

maria (sre): Post-incident plan: can we get a 60-min postmortem in 48 hours and a focused 30-min ops shareout after that (brown bag for learnings)? Proposed times: Thurs 15:00 UTC (postmortem), Fri 12:00 UTC (brown bag).

aj (runtime): I'm fine with Thurs. Action items I see: 1) revert/patch RBAC for autoscaler (kevin) 2) add canary test for autoscaler RBAC in infra CI (kevin/maria) 3) add runbook step to immediately split traffic to fallback models for degraded inference-pools (aj) 4) add alerting for controller 403 rate (maria).

kevin (infra): accepting INF-5234. timeline: will patch RBAC today and run a full rollout tomorrow to avoid another regression. I'll add the CI canary — INF-5235.

product-lead: also recommend we add automated customer-impact tag to incident page so CS can triage outreach. INF-5236 for ops automation.

oncall-sre: creating the postmortem doc now: https://docs.redwood.local/incidents/1837605120 — I'll record timeline, screenshots, and the logs we captured. assigning owners for action items there.

eng-learning: i'll host the brown bag if you want — focus on "Preventing control-plane regressions" and mitigation patterns for runtime teams. will prepare slides + a short demo of traffic split + runbook.

maria (sre): proposed owners + due dates in doc: RBAC patch (kevin) — due EOD+2, CI canary (kevin/maria) — due EOD+5, runbook update (aj) — due +3 days, controller 403 alert (maria) — due +2 days, customer outreach automation (product-lead) — due +7 days.

oncall-sre: for transparency, tagging this as follow-up on the weekly reliability review. please add any other items to the doc.

kevin (infra): quick note — i'm adding a small validation in the helm chart to reject RBAC changes without unit tests; will link PR in the doc.

ops-bot: Postmortem document created: https://docs.redwood.local/incidents/1837605120 — please comment with owner updates.

maria (sre): also adding a short retrospective note for platform engineering: consider defaulting fallback-model split to 5% when pool health drops > 20% as a safety net. open to debate on numbers.

aj (runtime): ACK — will prototype a safe-split controller for routes and add it to the runbook.

product-lead: CS will prepare a customer impact summary template — will attach to the postmortem so PM/CS knows who to reach out to and what to say.

eng-learning: scheduling brown bag: Fri 12:00 UTC — I'll book calendar and share a slide draft in #eng-learning. suggests 20min talk + 10 min Q&A.

oncall-sre: ok closing thread — thanks all for quick actions. follow-ups tracked in the postmortem doc and INF tickets.

incident-bot: Closing note: Incident 1837605120 -> mitigated -> postmortem scheduled. reminders: postmortem due in 48h, follow-ups assigned. :memo:
